big: Meena kept one page in a drawer, listing every account, policy and property, and where the papers are. After her mother's death, the family found everything in an afternoon, not in two years.

lines: What do I put in that list, and how often do I update it?
List every account, investment, policy and property, with how to claim each. Review it after big life events, and once a year as a habit.

intro: Small steps that help the most.
rows: A list of accounts, investments, policies and property
Where online accounts and recovery details are kept
Update nominations and wills after marriage, a child, divorce or a move
A lawyer and a tax adviser, since rules depend on facts
note: Keep the list safe, and tell one trusted person where it is. Do not write passwords in plain sight.

title: Keeping it organised
stops: An asset register lists accounts, policies and property
Nominations never need updating after a marriage
Online accounts count as assets family may need
Succession rules are the same for every family
caps: A single list saves a family months of searching.
Marriage, a child, divorce or a move all call for a review.
Note where login recovery details are kept, safely.
Rules depend on personal law and facts, so ask a professional.

q: Rohan has accounts in three banks and two fund houses. What helps his family most?
opts: No list, so no one gets confused
A list kept only in his head
A list shared on social media
why: No list leaves the family guessing and often missing assets.
A single list shows the family what exists and how to claim it.
A list in his head is lost when he is gone.
Social media makes private details public and invites fraud.

q: Meena has a new baby. What should she do about her nominations and will?
opts: Leave them as they are for ever
why: A big life event is the time to update her papers.
Old nominations may not match her wishes after a new child.
Cancelling policies would remove protection when it matters most.
A baby cannot be a witness to a will at all.

q: Dadi keeps her photos and email on cloud accounts. How can she help her family?
opts: Write every password on a postcard
Delete the accounts before her death
Tell no one that they exist
Note where recovery details are kept
why: Passwords on a postcard can be seen and misused.
Deleting accounts would lose what family may need to reach.
If no one knows of them, the family cannot find or access them.
A safe note on where recovery details are kept lets family gain access.

q: Why consult a lawyer and a tax adviser on succession?
opts: Because the rules are the same for all
Rules depend on law and family facts
Because the law forbids doing it yourself
why: The rules are not the same for all families, so this is wrong.
Advisers do not inherit the assets they advise on.
Personal law and family facts change what is right, so expert help matters.
The law does not forbid planning on your own, though advice lowers the risk.

pts: Keep one asset register: accounts, policies, property, and how to claim.
Review nominations and will after big life events.
Ask a lawyer and a tax adviser, since rules depend on the facts.
